9397afbbdf14d1f13fe38facb428e18adabd7a60.summary: This page is an event listing for a BrightTalk webcast, 'The Sample: Beating the Malware Pinata', presented by Christopher Gardner of the Mandiant FLARE reverse engineering team and published 2022-05-05. It outlines talk topics such as analysing droppers, extracting payloads from process injection, and open-source intelligence. It is an event and marketing page, not a threat report, so no facts are recorded.

930cc42115fcbd879cf67403b12c3a3e4e347abe.summary: Researcher's archived 2022 analysis of a Korean-language HWP document lure, attributed by the author to North Korea-linked APT37 and to its ROKRAT operations. A malicious HWP OLE object runs a BAT script that launches PowerShell to load shellcode into memory through reflective DLL injection. The shellcode stager was offline, so the in-memory payload was not analysed. The attribution is the author's own judgement.

hedges: The sample is from 2022; the author says it does not pertain to a known recent threat campaign, though the techniques covered may still apply.
The link to APT37 rests on the author's experience with the actor: 'this sample is related to APT37's ROKRAT operations'.
The exact relationship between the group and the North Korean state 'remains somewhat unclear'.
Coordination by the North Korean government is described as 'believed', not confirmed.
The shellcode stager was down when written up, so the in-memory payload was not analysed; the author assumes it would have resulted in ROKRAT.

936d216fd558bd4e58d2e486651504f4695378da.summary: Malpedia catalogue entry (Fraunhofer FKIE) for the Triton malware family, also called TRISIS or HatMan, which targets Triconex Safety Instrumented System controllers in industrial control systems. The entry lists the actor XENOTIME and a 2017 to 2022 timeline of references from FireEye, Dragos, NCCIC, CISA, FBI, Kaspersky, Nozomi Networks and the U.S. Treasury. A Russian government-owned lab attribution appears only as a FireEye reference title.
